children: Shares of Mumbai-based HDFC Bank Ltd., India's largest private sector lender, will be in focus on Monday, September 21, after global brokerage UBS retained its ‘Buy’ recommendation on the stock and added it to its APAC Key Call List.
UBS has set a price target of ₹1,000 for HDFC Bank, implying an upside of 36.8% from the stock's closing price of ₹731.20 on Friday.

The brokerage expects the uncertainty around the bank's leadership to be resolved in the coming weeks, following the submission of names to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for the chief executive officer position.

UBS believes some of the potential downside scenarios related to leadership uncertainty are already reflected in HDFC Bank's valuation. A resolution on the leadership front, therefore, could act as a catalyst for a re-rating of the stock, the brokerage said.

Beyond the leadership issue, UBS believes the market is underappreciating HDFC Bank's branch expansion over the past three to four years. The brokerage expects this expanded branch network to support stronger deposit growth in the years ahead and potentially allow HDFC Bank to gain ground on its peers.

Around 42% of HDFC Bank's branches are less than five years old, compared with roughly 5-30% for other large banks, according to UBS. As these newer branches mature, the brokerage expects their productivity to improve, providing further support to deposit mobilisation and overall business growth.

UBS has also seen early signs of a recovery in HDFC Bank's loan growth, which stood at 15.6% in Q1 FY27. The brokerage expects deposit growth to remain healthy, supported by measures taken by the RBI and improving liquidity conditions.

For FY27-FY29, UBS expects HDFC Bank's loan growth to improve towards 15%. It also expects the bank's net interest margin (NIM) to improve towards 3.5%, driven by faster growth in higher-yielding retail loans.
The brokerage expects HDFC Bank's return on assets (RoA) to improve to 1.9% in FY27 and FY28.
Given these expectations, UBS said the risk-reward profile of HDFC Bank appears favourable at 1.4 times its estimated FY28 price-to-book value (P/BV).
HDFC Bank also has broad analyst coverage. Of the 49 analysts tracked, 47 have a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, while two have a ‘Hold’ rating.
Shares of HDFC Bank closed 2.55% higher at ₹731.20 on Friday. Despite the recent gain, the stock remains down around 26% on a year-to-date basis.

title: HDFC Bank gets added to the UBS 'APAC Key Call List'; Here's why they are bullish
